key.why: Line 6 reads `cfg` with no lock held and no atomic, while line 12 may be writing it. Two accesses to the same non-atomic object, one of them a write, not ordered by anything: that is the definition of a data race.

readMore.title: Meyers & Alexandrescu: C++ and the Perils of Double-Checked Locking

lines.9: The `lock_guard` is correct, and it is doing what it says. A mutex orders the threads that take it against each other — it cannot order a thread that never takes it. Look for an access that is outside it.
lines.11: The second check is under the lock, together with the write, so those two are properly ordered against each other. That much of the idiom is right.
lines.12: The write is under the lock, so it is ordered against every other access that also takes the lock. The problem is an access that does not.
lines.14: This return is under the lock, so the read it does is fine.

feedback.nudge: List every line that touches `cfg` and mark which of them hold the mutex. The race is between a pair, and one of that pair is unprotected.
